header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are the integrating analyst of a code-safety review. Six departments have each committed `findings/<department>.json` and `report/<department>.md` on their own branch, and this worktree is the merge of all of them. You write two files and nothing else: `findings.json` and `SAFETY-REPORT.md`.

Read `REPORTING.md` in this worktree first: it states the finding format, the exact sections of the report, the count lines both summaries carry, and the certificate's wording. Read `target.json` for the tree under review and the SHA-256 the certificate states. Read every `findings/*.json` and every `report/*.md` before writing anything. When a `report-template` skill is available, load it: it owns how the report reads, while `REPORTING.md` owns what the examiner mechanically decides and wins wherever the two differ in form.

Ask the examiner which findings do not hold before you write the union:

    for f in findings/*.json; do node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings "$f" --list-invalid; done

Every id it prints is dropped from `findings.json` and named under `## What was not covered`, with the reason. Dropping one silently fails the report.

`findings.json` is the union, deduplicated by `file` plus `line` plus `cwe`, keeping the entry whose `confidence` is higher. Copy each entry whole; do not rewrite a department's `snippet`, because the examiner compares it with the target's own text.

The report is a review by a language model, grounded by a static scanner and by the committed examiner, over the files the departments actually read. `## Scope and method` says that, names the departments that ran and the tools that ran, and states what was read rather than what exists. `## What was not covered` is not a formality: name the file kinds nobody opened, the classes of defect no department owns, the checks that did not run, and every dropped finding. Never write that the target is secure, safe or free of vulnerabilities — nothing this program did could support it, and the examiner refuses the claim.

Before you stop, run `node verify-safety-report.mjs --report`, fix every line it names, and commit everything. Work left uncommitted is not delivered and is not measured. Never write into the target tree, and never edit `verify-safety-report.mjs`, `target.json` or any department's committed files.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one is sampled across top-level entries, so it spans the tree instead of one subtree.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result instead returns 100 paths sampled across top-level entries, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

<skill_instructions>
# The report layout

Every report has exactly these sections, in this order. Do not add marketing language, severity totals presented as a score out of ten, or a remediation timeline the review has no authority to commit the customer to.

- **`## Résumé exécutif`** — French. Counts per severity, the three most important findings by name and effect, what was and was not covered in one sentence each, and one paragraph on method.
- **`## Executive summary`** — the same content in English, for a mixed-language or non-French reader.
- **`## Scope and method`** — the repository, commit or tag reviewed, which directories or services were in scope, and a link to [review-method](../review-method/SKILL.md).
- **`## Findings`** — grouped by severity, critical first; one bullet per finding with its id, title, `file:line`, CWE, and confidence. Full detail (snippet, evidence, impact, fix) lives in the accompanying JSON per [severity-and-evidence](../severity-and-evidence/SKILL.md), not duplicated in prose here.
- **`## What was not covered`** — the [review-method](../review-method/SKILL.md) not-covered list, specific to this engagement.
- **`## Certificate`** — what a mechanical verifier checked after the fact: every finding resolves to a real file and line in the reviewed commit, every id is unique, every CWE/OWASP id is a known identifier, and no two findings share file, line, and CWE. This certifies the report's internal consistency, not the completeness or correctness of the review's judgment.

## Filled example: a small Express app

```markdown
## Résumé exécutif

Cette revue a porté sur le code source de commande-api, une application Express.js
de gestion de commandes, au commit a1b2c3d. Elle a permis d'identifier 3 constats :
1 critique, 1 moyen et 1 faible. Les plus importants : (1) une injection SQL
critique dans la recherche de commande par identifiant (src/routes/orders.js:42),
permettant de lire ou modifier toute donnée accessible par l'utilisateur de base de
données de l'application ; (2) une fixation de session lors de la connexion
(src/routes/auth.js:58) ; (3) l'absence de l'en-tête HSTS (src/app.js:12). La revue
a couvert les points d'entrée HTTP, l'authentification et la gestion des sessions ;
elle n'a pas couvert l'infrastructure de déploiement ni les dépendances tierces
(voir « Ce qui n'a pas été couvert »). Méthode : lecture des points d'entrée,
suivi des données de la source jusqu'au point d'exécution, un constat par point
d'exécution, ligne exactement citée et niveau de confiance déclaré pour chacun.

## Executive summary

This review covered commande-api, an Express.js order-management application, at
commit a1b2c3d, and found 3 issues: 1 critical, 1 medium, 1 low. The most
important: (1) a critical SQL injection in order lookup by id
(src/routes/orders.js:42); (2) session fixation on login
(src/routes/auth.js:58); (3) a missing HSTS header (src/app.js:12). HTTP entry
points, authentication, and session handling were covered; deployment
infrastructure and third-party dependencies were not (see "What was not covered").

## Scope and method

Repository commande-api, commit a1b2c3d, `src/` only. Method: [review-method](../review-method/SKILL.md).

## Findings

### Critical
- SEC-001 — SQL injection in order lookup — `src/routes/orders.js:42` — CWE-89 — confirmed

### Medium
- SEC-002 — Session id not rotated after login (session fixation) — `src/routes/auth.js:58` — CWE-384 — likely

### Low
- SEC-003 — Missing Strict-Transport-Security header — `src/app.js:12` — CWE-319 — confirmed

## What was not covered

- `infra/` (Terraform, Dockerfiles) and CI/CD configuration.
- Third-party dependency advisories (separate engagement).
- Runtime configuration: actual deployed environment variables, WAF rules, and network topology.
- Native mobile or memory-safety classes of bug: this codebase has no native module.

## Certificate

Mechanically verified: 3/3 findings resolve to an existing line at commit a1b2c3d;
3/3 ids unique; 3/3 CWE and OWASP ids recognized; 0 findings share file, line, and
CWE. This certifies internal consistency only, not completeness of coverage.
```

# Severity, evidence, and the finding schema

## Severity rubric

Score by the worst realistic case the code as read supports, not the theoretical worst case of the vulnerability class in general.

| Severity | Exploitability | Auth required | Data affected | Blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Critical** | Remote, no user interaction, reliable | None, or any authenticated user | Full database, all tenants, or code execution | Entire system or every tenant |
| **High** | Remote, at most one minor precondition (a known id, a low-privilege account) | None or low-privileged | One tenant's full data, or a horizontal slice across many | One tenant, or many via a shared flaw |
| **Medium** | Needs user interaction (a clicked link, an opened file) or a specific role | Authenticated, often a specific role | A user's data beyond their own, or a narrow field set | One user or a small group |
| **Low** | Needs substantial preconditions (local access, a race window, non-default config) | Elevated access already, or local access | Limited or already-authorized data | Single record, with another control still present |
| **Info** | No exploit path demonstrated in the code read | N/A | N/A | Hardening gap, or a `possible`-confidence pattern needing more context |

## The evidence rule

Every finding's evidence names, in prose: the exact reachable source (which entry point, which parameter), every step the tainted value passes through with its file and line, the sink, and why no guard on that path stops it (or which guard was checked and found absent). "This looks like SQL injection" is not evidence; "`req.params.id` from the route at line 40 reaches the template literal at line 42 with no parameterization" is.

## The finding schema

```json
{
  "id": "SEC-001",
  "cwe": "CWE-89",
  "owasp": "A05:2025 / A03:2021",
  "severity": "critical",
  "confidence": "confirmed",
  "title": "SQL injection in order lookup via string-concatenated query",
  "file": "src/routes/orders.js",
```

"evidence": "config here is the merged object built at line 10 from config/env/all.js and the environment file, which includes cookieSecret: \"session_cookie_secret_key_here\" and cryptoKey: \"a_secure_key_for_crypto_here\" (config/env/all.js lines 8-9). util.inspect(config, false, null) prints every own property with no depth limit, so both secrets land in stdout, and from there in whatever process manager or log aggregator captures it, on every single process start.",

"impact": "Anyone with read access to the server's console output, process logs, or a log-shipping pipeline (operators, a misconfigured log bucket, a compromised sidecar) obtains the session-signing secret and can forge session cookies for any user.",
"fix": "Remove this startup dump, or redact known-sensitive keys (cookieSecret, cryptoKey) before logging, and log to a controlled sink rather than stdout by default.",
"title": "NODE_ENV silently defaults to \"development\" when unset, and the production config file adds no hardening at all",

"evidence": "When NODE_ENV is not set, config.js loads config/env/development.js, whose environmentalScripts array (lines 9-13) injects an extra <script> tag with a livereload connection into every page rendered through app/views/layout.html (line 125-127), and config/env/production.js (module.exports = {}) is an empty stub that overrides nothing, so \"production\" mode is not materially different from the base config either. docker-compose.yml only declares NODE_ENV: with no value (line 7), so a deployment started with docker-compose up and no NODE_ENV exported on the host inherits this development fallback. "impact": "A deployment that forgets to export NODE_ENV=production runs with development settings live, including the injected livereload script tag on every authenticated page, and gets none of the (currently nonexistent) production-only hardening, silently and without any error.",

"title": "The global error handler renders the raw Error object into the HTML response",

"evidence": "This is the app-wide error middleware registered last in app/routes/index.js (app.use(ErrorHandler), line 82), so every unhandled error in any route reaches it. It logs err.stack server-side (line 8, correct) but also passes the whole err object as error into error-template.html, whose only content is
{{error}} (line 11), which stringifies the Error (at minimum its message, e.g. Mongo driver or validation error text). swig's autoescape is disabled globally in server.js (autoescape: false, line 137), so whatever that string contains is written into the response unescaped.",

"impact": "Internal error messages (library names, query/validation detail) reach the client on any unhandled exception, helping an attacker map the backend, and because output is unescaped, an error message containing HTML-significant characters is reflected without encoding.",
"fix": "Log err.stack server-side only, and render a fixed generic message plus a correlation id to the client instead of the error object itself.",
"title": "POST /login has no rate limiting or lockout, and passwords are compared in plaintext",

"evidence": "No limiter middleware is attached to this route or mounted globally in server.js; package.json has no rate-limiting dependency (express-rate-limit or similar) and a repository-wide search for cors|rate-limit|ratelimit|limiter finds nothing in the app's own code. handleLoginRequest (app/routes/session.js line 53) calls userDAO.validateLogin, whose comparePassword (app/data/user-dao.js line 60-61) is a plain fromDB === fromUser string comparison with bcrypt.compareSync commented out at line 65, and there is no failed-attempt counter anywhere in user-dao.js.",

"fix": "Add a rate limiter (express-rate-limit or similar) keyed by username and IP in front of POST /login and POST /signup, and add an account lockout or exponential backoff after repeated failures.",

3: ## Résumé exécutif
4: 
5: Cette revue a porté sur NodeGoat, une application Express.js/MongoDB délibérément
6: vulnérable (OWASP), au sein de l'arborescence verrouillée `/home/user/targets/NodeGoat`
7: (111 fichiers). Le département « access » a construit la table complète des routes
8: enregistrées dans `app/routes/index.js` et lu, pour chacune, la chaîne de middlewares
9: qui la précède, avant de suivre les données depuis la requête jusqu'au point d'accès
10: aux données ou à la session. Huit constats ont été retenus, tous en confiance
11: « confirmed » : 4 de sévérité haute et 4 de sévérité moyenne, aucun critique ni
12: faible. Les trois plus importants : (1) la page `/allocations/:userId`
13: (`app/routes/index.js:63`) charge les allocations financières d'un autre employé à
14: partir d'un identifiant pris tel quel dans l'URL, sans jamais le comparer à
15: `req.session.userId` — une référence directe non protégée ; (2) la route
16: `POST /benefits` (`app/routes/index.js:56`) permet à n'importe quel utilisateur
17: authentifié, pas seulement un administrateur, de modifier la date de début des
18: avantages sociaux d'un autre employé, le contrôle de rôle `isAdmin` existant dans
19: le code étant présent mais commenté sur cette route ; (3) la connexion
20: (`app/routes/session.js:116`) ne régénère jamais l'identifiant de session après
21: authentification, exposant l'application à une fixation de session, alors que la
22: route d'inscription voisine le fait correctement. Semgrep (règles locales du
23: paquet + `p/owasp-top-ten`) a été exécuté sur l'arbre entier ; chacun de ses 29
24: résultats a servi de point de lecture, aucun n'a été reporté tel quel comme
25: constat. Cette revue ne couvre ni l'exécution réelle du serveur, ni les
26: dépendances tierces, ni les autres départements (injection, données, secrets).

34: ## Executive summary
35: 
36: This review covered NodeGoat, a deliberately vulnerable Express.js/MongoDB
37: application, over the locked tree at `/home/user/targets/NodeGoat` (111 files).
38: The access department built the full route table registered in
39: `app/routes/index.js`, read the exact middleware chain in front of every route,
40: and traced request data forward to its sink (a database query or a session
41: write) for each one. Eight findings were kept, all at `confirmed` confidence: 4

1: # Injection and traversal review — NodeGoat
2: 
3: ## Scope and method
4: 
5: Target: `/home/user/targets/NodeGoat`, 111 files locked by `target.json` (sha256 `78ac112b7bd5083bb065086c4642dcd8a3932a8d3052f9405503124c90a70fe3`). This is a review by a language model, grounded by a static scanner (semgrep) and by the mechanical examiner `verify-safety-report.mjs`; it is not a proof of absence of vulnerabilities.
6: 
7: `semgrep --version` reported `1.177.0`, so semgrep ran: `semgrep --config <local code-safety.yml> --config p/owasp-top-ten --metrics off --json` over the target tree. The registry pack (`p/owasp-top-ten`) was reachable, so both the local rules and the registry pack ran together — 113 rules total across 72 git-tracked files, 29 raw hits. Every semgrep hit was read as a lead, not taken as a finding on its own; several (the `express-cookie-settings` family, the hardcoded-secret hits in `config/env/*`, the GitHub Actions mutable-tag warnings, the plaintext-HTTP links in the tutorial pages) belong to other departments (secrets, platform, dependencies) and are left for them.
8: 
9: For each remaining lead, I read the full path by hand: the Express route table (`app/routes/index.js`), every route handler under `app/routes/`, every DAO under `app/data/`, the relevant Swig templates under `app/views/`, and the template-engine setup in `server.js`. I traced each candidate sink backward to `req.query`, `req.body`, or `req.session` and forward to confirm what actually renders or executes it, reading intermediate functions rather than assuming their behavior from their names, per the department's review method.
10: 
11: Files read in full: `server.js`, `app/routes/index.js`, `app/routes/{allocations,benefits,contributions,error,memos,profile,research,session,tutorial}.js`, `app/data/{allocations,benefits,contributions,memos,profile,research,user}-dao.js`, `app/views/{profile,memos}.html`, and `package.json` for dependency versions referenced in evidence.
12: 
13: ## What was found
14: 
15: Six sinks were confirmed or judged likely reachable from request data with no guard in between:
16: 
17: 1. **`app/routes/contributions.js:32-34`** — `eval()` on `req.body.preTax`/`afterTax`/`roth` (CWE-95, critical, confirmed). Full server-side code execution for any authenticated user.
18: 2. **`app/data/allocations-dao.js:78`** — MongoDB `$where` built by interpolating `req.query.threshold` into a JavaScript string (CWE-943, high, confirmed).
19: 3. **`app/routes/research.js:15-16`** — outbound HTTP request built by concatenating `req.query.url` and `req.query.symbol`, then fetched server-side with `needle.get()` and streamed back to the client (CWE-918 SSRF, high, confirmed).
20: 4. **`app/routes/index.js:72`** — `res.redirect(req.query.url)` with no destination check (CWE-601 open redirect, medium, confirmed).
21: 5. **`app/views/profile.html:41`** — reflected XSS: `req.body.firstName` reaches this `{{ }}` output unescaped because `server.js:137` globally disables Swig's autoescaping (CWE-79, medium, confirmed).
22: 6. **`app/views/memos.html:31`** — every user's stored memo is rendered through `marked()` in the same unescaped template context; the app relies on `marked`'s deprecated `sanitize: true` option rather than a maintained HTML sanitizer, and I did not verify that option resists every markdown-syntax XSS vector in `marked` 0.3.5, so this is `likely` rather than `confirmed` (CWE-79, high).
23: 
24: Full detail, evidence, and fixes for each are in `findings/injection.json`.
25: 
26: ## What was not covered
27: 
28: - **Non-application files**: vendored front-end libraries (`app/assets/vendor/*`), build tooling (`Gruntfile.js`), and CI workflows were scanned by semgrep but not read line-by-line for injection sinks, since they are not part of the request-handling path.
29: - **`test/` and `artifacts/`**: the e2e/Cypress specs, the security test harness (`test/security/profile-test.js`), and `artifacts/db-reset.js` were not traced as entry points; they run outside the deployed request path.
30: - **`app/routes/session.js`, `app/routes/benefits.js`, `app/routes/tutorial.js`**: opened and skimmed for sinks matching this department's list (no string-built queries, `eval`, or unescaped raw-HTML output found), but not traced field-by-field to the same depth as the six sinks above, since they use structured MongoDB filters (`benefits-dao.js`) or static tutorial content only.
31: - **The full extent of the global-autoescape-off finding**: disabling Swig autoescaping (`server.js:137`) affects *every* `{{ }}` expression in every `.html` view, not only the two cited here. `app/views/profile.html` alone reflects `lastName`, `ssn`, `dob`, `address`, `bankAcc`, and `bankRouting` the same way; these are not listed as separate findings because they share the same root cause and confirmation would be repetitive, but a full remediation must re-enable autoescaping globally, not patch line 41 alone.
32: - **`marked` 0.3.5's actual sanitizer behavior**: I read that `sanitize: true` is configured and that autoescape is off, but did not read `marked`'s own source to confirm which markdown constructs its sanitizer fails to neutralize; finding 6 is marked `likely` for exactly this reason.
33: - **Runtime/deployment configuration**: no WAF, reverse proxy, or CSP was assumed to exist or to mitigate any of these findings, because none is configured in this repository (`server.js` serves plain HTTP with no `helmet` CSP in the injection-relevant paths); this review only confirms what the application code itself does.
34: - **SQL injection**: NodeGoat's persistence layer is exclusively MongoDB via the native driver; no SQL string-building code exists in the tree, so CWE-89 is not applicable here and no finding was forced to fit it.
35: - **Command injection and path traversal**: grepped for `child_process`, `exec`/`execSync`/`spawn`, `fs.*`, and `sendFile` across the tree; the only hits are literal, non-request-derived paths (TLS certificate loading in `server.js:25-26`, build-script execution in `Gruntfile.js`, and test fixtures), so neither class produced a finding.

(End of file - total 35 lines)

Seven findings, all `confidence: confirmed` — each cites a line that was read, and the line the software that consumes it was also read.

1. **secrets-cookie-secret** (`config/env/all.js:8`, CWE-798, **high**) — the express-session signing secret is the literal `"session_cookie_secret_key_here"`, merged into every environment (production.js is empty) and passed straight to `express-session` in `server.js:82` with no environment override anywhere. Anyone with this repository can forge a session cookie for any user, including the admin.

2. **secrets-admin-password-plaintext** (`artifacts/db-reset.js:18`, CWE-798/CWE-259, **critical**) — the admin account is seeded with the plaintext literal `"Admin_123"` by a script wired into both the Docker Compose startup command (`docker-compose.yml:9`) and the Heroku `postdeploy` hook (`app.json:13`). `app/data/user-dao.js:60-61` validates logins with a plaintext `fromDB === fromUser` comparison, so this seeded password is a live, working admin credential on any deployment that used the default reset step.

3. **secrets-committed-rsa-private-key** (`artifacts/cert/server.key:1-15`, CWE-321, **medium**) — a complete, parseable RSA private key is committed at the exact path the commented-out HTTPS block in `server.js:21-27` reads for its TLS key. The live server currently only starts plain HTTP, so this key is not loaded by the code that runs today, but it is exposed to every reader of the repository and is the key that would serve HTTPS the moment that block is restored.

4. **secrets-config-logged-to-console** (`config/config.js:12-13`, CWE-532, **medium**) — the fully merged config object, including `cookieSecret` and `cryptoKey`, is dumped to stdout via `console.log(util.inspect(config, ...))` on every process start, so both secrets land in whatever captures stdout (CI logs, `docker logs`, Heroku's log stream).

5 & 6. **secrets-zap-api-key-development** / **secrets-zap-api-key-test** (`config/env/development.js:6`, `config/env/test.js:6`, CWE-798, **low**) — the same OWASP ZAP API key (`v9dn0balpqas1pcc281tn5ood1`) is hard-coded in both environment files and consumed by more than a dozen live `zaproxy` client calls in `test/security/profile-test.js`. Confirmed as a real, used credential, but scoped to a local security-scanning proxy on `192.168.56.20:8080`, not to production data — a test-tooling secret, not a production one.

7. **secrets-dead-crypto-key** (`config/env/all.js:9`, CWE-321, **low**) — the AES key literal `"a_secure_key_for_crypto_here"` is exported by the config module, but its only would-be consumer (`app/data/profile-dao.js`'s encrypt/decrypt helpers) is entirely commented out, so SSN/DOB fields are stored in plaintext today and no data is currently encrypted with this key. It is flagged at low severity because it is a real, non-placeholder secret shipped in config and reproduced verbatim in the tutorial page `app/views/tutorial/a6.html:83` as the "correct" key to use, meaning re-enabling the documented fix would put real encryption behind a key every reader already has.

- **Dependency-level secrets**: `package-lock.json` was not scanned entry-by-entry for embedded registry tokens or auth URLs; no `.npmrc` exists in the tree so this risk is limited, but transitive package sources were not audited.

- **Git history**: this review read only the working tree at the locked commit (`target.json`'s file list and hashes); it did not run a full-history scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog) to check whether a rotated secret still exists in an earlier blob, because the target is a fixed, read-only tree without accessible history in this session.

- **Runtime/deployment secrets**: actual production values of `MONGODB_URI`, `PORT`, or `NODE_ENV` as set on a real deployment (Heroku config vars, container environment) were not observed; only the source defaults were read. `config/env/all.js:3` does read `MONGODB_URI` from the environment with a localhost fallback — the fallback is a local, unauthenticated MongoDB URL and not itself a credential leak, so it was not raised as a separate finding.

- **Binary/vendored assets**: `app/assets/vendor/**` (jQuery, Bootstrap, Raphael, Morris, FontAwesome) and image/font binaries were not inspected for embedded secrets; they are third-party vendored libraries, not application configuration.

- **Non-secrets vulnerability classes**: injection, XSS, authorization, and session-management bugs visible in the same files (e.g. the plaintext password comparison in `user-dao.js`, the disabled CSRF/helmet protections in `server.js`) are real but out of scope for this department's report; they are noted here only where they establish that a secret is a *working* credential.

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
3: // repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
4: //
5: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path>  one department's findings
6: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path> --list-invalid
7: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --report           the merged report
8: //
9: // `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
10: // `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
11: // stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
12: // learns which findings to drop and disclose.
13: //
14: // `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
15: // disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
16: // findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
17: //
18: // Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
19: // stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
20: // this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
21: import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
22: import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
23: import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
24: 
25: /** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
26: const SEVERITIES = ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info']
27: 
28: /** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
29: const CONFIDENCES = ['confirmed', 'likely', 'possible']
30: 
31: /** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
32: const SECTIONS = [
33:   '## Résumé exécutif',
34:   '## Executive summary',
35:   '## Scope and method',
36:   '## Findings',
37:   '## What was not covered',
38:   '## Certificate',
39: ]
40: 
41: /** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */
42: const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
43: 
44: /** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
45: const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
46: 
47: /** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
48: const PLACEHOLDER = /\bTODO\b|\bTBD\b|\bFIXME\b|lorem ipsum|<placeholder>|PLACEHOLDER/i
49: 
50: /** String fields every finding states in prose. */
51: const PROSE_FIELDS = ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'fix']
52: 
53: /** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
54: const normalize = (text) => text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
55: 
56: /** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
57: const sha256 = (content) => createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
61:  * @param {string} root directory to walk
62:  * @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
63:  * @returns {string[]} relative POSIX-ish paths, sorted
64:  */
65: function walk(root, exclude) {
66:   const found = []
67:   const descend = (directory) => {
68:     for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
69:       const path = join(directory, entry.name)
70:       if (entry.isDirectory()) {
71:         if (!exclude.includes(entry.name)) descend(path)
72:       } else if (entry.isFile()) found.push(relative(root, path))
73:     }
74:   }
75:   descend(root)
76:   return found.sort()
77: }
78: 
79: /** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
80: class Target {
81:   /**
82:    * @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
83:    * @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
84:    */
85:   constructor(reportRoot, failures) {
86:     this.failures = failures
87:     this.root = undefined
88:     this.files = new Map()
89:     this.lines = new Map()
90:     const lockPath = join(reportRoot, 'target.json')
91:     if (!existsSync(lockPath)) {
92:       failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
93:       return
94:     }
95:     const lock = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8'))
96:     this.root = lock.root
97:     this.exclude = lock.exclude ?? []
98:     this.digest = lock.sha256
99:     for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
100:     this.checkTree()
101:   }
102: 
103:   /**
104:    * Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
105:    * cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
106:    * department edited is no longer that tree.
107:    */
108:   checkTree() {
109:     if (!existsSync(this.root)) {
110:       this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
111:       this.root = undefined
112:       return
113:     }
114:     const present = walk(this.root, this.exclude)
115:     for (const path of present) {
116:       if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
117:     }
118:     for (const [path, hash] of this.files) {
119:       if (!present.includes(path)) {
120:         this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
121:         continue
122:       }
123:       if (sha256(readFileSync(join(this.root, path))) !== hash) {
124:         this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
125:       }
126:     }
127:   }
128: 
129:   /**
130:    * The lines of one target file.
131:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
132:    * @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
133:    */
134:   linesOf(path) {
135:     if (this.root === undefined || !this.files.has(path)) return undefined
136:     if (!this.lines.has(path)) this.lines.set(path, readFileSync(join(this.root, path), 'utf8').split('\n'))
137:     return this.lines.get(path)
138:   }
139: 
140:   /**
141:    * Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
142:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
143:    * @param {number} line 1-based line number
144:    * @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
145:    */
146:   resolves(path, line) {
147:     const lines = this.linesOf(path)
148:     return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: /**
153:  * Decide one finding against the target tree.
154:  * @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
155:  * @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
156:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
157:  * @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
158:  * @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
159:  */
160: function checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen) {
161:   const failures = []
162:   if (finding === null || typeof finding !== 'object' || Array.isArray(finding)) {
163:     return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
164:   }
165:   const id = finding.id
166:   const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
167:   const fail = (rule) => void failures.push(`${name}: ${rule}`)
168:   // Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
169:   // numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
170:   if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
171:   else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
172:   else seen.add(id)
173:   if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
174:   if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
175:   if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
176:   if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
177:   for (const field of PROSE_FIELDS) {
178:     if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
179:   }
180:   if (!Array.isArray(finding.references) || finding.references.some(reference => typeof reference !== 'string')) {
181:     fail('references must be an array of strings')
182:   }
183:   const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
184:   if (typeof file !== 'string' || file === '' || file.startsWith('/') || file.split('/').includes('..')) {
185:     fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
186:     return failures
187:   }
188:   const lines = target.linesOf(file)
189:   if (lines === undefined) {
190:     fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
191:     return failures
192:   }
193:   if (!Number.isInteger(line) || line < 1 || line > lines.length) {
194:     fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
195:     return failures
196:   }
197:   const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
198:   if (!Number.isInteger(last) || last < line || last > lines.length) {
199:     fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
200:     return failures
201:   }
202:   if (typeof snippet !== 'string' || snippet.trim() === '') {
203:     fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
204:     return failures
205:   }
206:   const quoted = normalize(lines.slice(line - 1, last).join('\n'))
207:   if (normalize(snippet) !== quoted) {

"evidence": "addUser() builds the user document with the raw `password` parameter taken directly from the signup request body (app/routes/session.js handleSignup -> userDAO.addUser(userName, firstName, lastName, password, email, ...)) and inserts it unmodified via usersCol.insert(user, ...) at line 45. The bcrypt hashing call (`password: bcrypt.hashSync(password, bcrypt.genSaltSync())`) is present only inside the comment block at lines 26-30 and is never executed. validateLogin()'s comparePassword at line 61 (`return fromDB === fromUser;`) confirms the stored value is compared as plaintext, not through bcrypt.compareSync (also commented out at line 65). Every account's password is therefore held in the `users` collection exactly as submitted.",

"impact": "Anyone who can read the `users` collection - via a database backup, an administrator, or the NoSQL injection already reachable through the $where query in app/data/allocations-dao.js - obtains every user's real login password in plaintext, not a hash, enabling immediate account takeover on this application and on any other service where the same password is reused.",

"fix": "Hash passwords with bcrypt (or argon2id) before insert, e.g. `password: bcrypt.hashSync(password, bcrypt.genSaltSync(12))`, and compare with `bcrypt.compareSync(fromUser, fromDB)` in validateLogin instead of `===`.",
"title": "underscore resolves to 1.9.1, inside the range for a template-injection RCE and an unbounded-recursion DoS",

Neither advisory required tracing this project's own call sites; both are matched on the resolved version directly.",

"impact": "Any code path in this app or its dependency graph that renders an underscore template with attacker-influenced content lets an attacker run arbitrary JavaScript in the Node process; a crafted object handed to the affected utility functions can also crash the process via stack exhaustion.",
"fix": "Upgrade underscore to >=1.13.7 (the declared ^1.8.3 range does not permit this; the manifest range itself must be raised), then re-run npm audit to confirm the range clears both advisories.",

## Executive summary

This review covers OWASP NodeGoat, a deliberately vulnerable Express.js/MongoDB
application, over the locked tree at `/home/user/targets/NodeGoat` (111 files, sha256
`78ac112b7bd5083bb065086c4642dcd8a3932a8d3052f9405503124c90a70fe3`). Six departments
read the code (access, data, dependencies, injection, platform, secrets), each using
`semgrep 1.177.0` (the local department rule pack plus `p/owasp-top-ten`) and, for the
dependencies department, `npm audit` against the live npm registry; every tool hit was
treated as a lead to read, never reported as a finding on its own strength. The
integration merged all six `findings/<department>.json` files, deduplicated by file +
line + CWE, and verified every retained finding with the mechanical examiner
`verify-safety-report.mjs`, which confirms every cited `file:line` exists in the locked
tree and that the quoted snippet matches the real text. 38 findings are retained: 4
critical, 16 high, 14 medium, 4 low. The three most important: (1) server-side code
injection via `eval()` on submitted contribution percentages
(`app/routes/contributions.js:32`), giving any authenticated user arbitrary JavaScript
execution inside the Node process; (2) every account's password is stored and compared
in cleartext, never hashed (`app/data/user-dao.js:25`); (3) the admin account is seeded
with a hard-coded plaintext password (`artifacts/db-reset.js:18`) that the live login
path accepts as-is. Nine duplicate findings (same file, line, and CWE, written
independently by two departments) were folded into one each; the id dropped from each
pair is listed under "What was not covered". This review is a static read by a
language model, grounded by a static analyzer and by the committed mechanical
examiner; it does not cover runtime behavior, git history, or the full transitive
dependency tree.
